Examples: clause introducers/complementizers, verbs or auxiliaries lacking their object/complement, negation or modality, contrastives (but/however), and list enumerators. If yes, raise Contra (near 1.0) even if surface cohesion looks good; compute target = cohesion × (1 − contra) and let high Contra drive the target down.

- Determines whether the continuation forces reinterpreting who, what, or whether an event occurred; for example, when a later clause negates, restricts, or changes the referent. Cuts that leave earlier material liable to reversal should score low on this judgement.

- Tests whether splitting the sentence separates dependents or attachments: modifiers, relative clauses, objects/complements, possessives, or prepositional phrases that belong to the other side. Also watch scope-bearing elements (negation, auxiliaries) and narrow-focus adverbials. If independent translation would orphan or misattach constituents, cohesion must be reduced.
Apply both judgements at every inter-word position. Treat punctuation as attached to the preceding word and follow the corpus rule that certain punctuation characters never start a segment.

Provisional-head test: At each marker ask whether the left span ends with a head that makes a listener commit to a concrete interpretation the immediate continuation can reverse, restrict, or complete. If yes, set Contra high (near 1.0) even if surface cohesion looks good; compute target = cohesion × (1 − contra) so high Contra drives the target down.
